sara: heads up — na-west started dropping egress to a subset of our edge POPs around 15:02 UTC. auto dns failover kicked but we have asymmetric cache behavior across resolvers. seeing ~40% reduction in available GPU capacity for na-west pools.

michael: do we know which records flipped? low TTLs configured for failover but caches still returning native na-west in some regions.

alert-bot: [AUTO] 1719904321 - DNS failover policy applied for service redwood-inference.prod -> weight shift na-west:70% -> na-east:30% (policy: emergency-failover-v2).

ben: quick dig from my laptop shows mixed answers. some resolvers still returning na-west A, others na-east. digging with EDNS-client-subnet shows edge-specific variation.

ben: paste: ```
$ dig +short redwood-inference.prod.edge.example.net @8.8.8.8
52.12.34.56
$ dig +short redwood-inference.prod.edge.example.net @1.1.1.1
34.210.111.22
```

julia: that matches the split-horizon cache issue i've seen before — CDNs and some ISPs ignore low TTLs or have min-ttl clamps. we should treat DNS as eventual and plan for in-flight traffic mismatch.

ryan-oncall: ops checklist: 1) confirm origin routing + health checks 2) force purge at CDN providers for the A records 3) update LB weights for session-aware proxies 4) slow-roll traffic via policy to avoid thundering herd. anyone on purges?

sara: purges started on FastEdge + GlobalCache. submitted ticket to provider to flush authoritative caches and asked to short-circuit TTL clamping. also kicked a job to drain sessions on na-west GPU pool gracefully.

michael: note on TTL tuning — lowering TTL to 30s helps future events but doesn't retroactively clear caches. we should avoid setting <30s permanently due to DNS query cost. propose temp-30s during incidents then revert to 300s baseline.

ben: agreement. also enabling our smart-routing fallback so new sessions prefer na-east until na-west capacity >80%. that avoids overloading warm-up buckets.

julia: observed a spike in cold-start provisioning when traffic shifted. provisioning queued ~120 pods for GPU backfill, taking ~8-12 mins on node spin-up. suggestion: pre-warm burst capacity in Dedicated pool for critical tiers.

ryan-oncall: cost callout — pre-warm burst or use reserved spare GPUs will add ~$1800/hr if we maintain full cold-surge reserve in prod. for emergency-only pre-warm we can set a small cap (~10 GPUs) ~ $220/hr. which do we want?

sara: for now enable small cap (10) to reduce cold start pressure and maintain latency SLOs. create follow-up for finance to evaluate monthly tradeoffs.

alert-bot: [NOTIFICATION] CDN purge submitted (ticket #CDN-5428). authoritative flush requested.

michael: one more technical: some resolvers clamp TTLs to a provider minimum (often 300s). for future incidents we should: (a) tag failover records with a short-lived CNAME chain we can control TTL for, (b) implement weighted LB at the anycast edge to avoid reliance on public resolver churn.

julia: +1 on CNAME trick and edge weights. also add a step to incident runbook: "if caches are inconsistent after failover, do not manually flip global DNS again; instead shift edge weights and purge caches." saves churn.

ben: i've posted a small dig/verify script in #eng-tools to help oncall quickly check resolver variation: `scripts/dig-resolvers.sh redwood-inference.prod` — run across multiple resolvers/regions.

ryan-oncall: status update: na-west capacity slowly recovering after draining and node reboots; GPU pool at 65% healthy. CDN providers acknowledged cache flush but some ISPs still returning old answers ~10-12 mins TTL clamp. monitoring.

sara: thanks all. next actions: 1) keep small pre-warm cap enabled (ops ticket), 2) add TTL/CNAME pattern to runbook, 3) run post-incident analysis on propagation window and cost impact. i'll own the PIR.

michael: note for PIR: quantify token loss, rate-limited retries, and estimate cost of burst pre-warm vs. outage impact.

alert-bot: [AUTO] thread archived for incident 1719904321 after initial stabilization.
